GAMR: A Guided Attention Model for (Visual) Reasoning
publications.abstract: A novel module for visual reasoning that instantiates an active-vision theory — solving complex visual reasoning dynamically via sequences of attention shifts that route task-relevant information into memory. GAMR learns visual routines robustly and sample-efficiently, and generalizes zero-shot to novel reasoning tasks.

publications.title: PhD Thesis: Exploring the Role of (Self-)Attention in Cognitive and Computer Vision Architecture
publications.venue: Université Paul Sabatier (Toulouse III) / Brown University / ANITI
publications.abstract: Investigates the role of attention and memory in complex reasoning. Analyses Transformer self-attention, extends it with memory, refines the taxonomy of SVRT reasoning tasks, and proposes GAMR — a cognitive architecture combining attention and memory inspired by active-vision theory.

publications.title: A Benchmark for Compositional Visual Reasoning
publications.authors: Aimen Zerroug, Mohit Vaishnav, Julien Colin, Sebastian Musslick, Thomas Serre
publications.abstract: Introduces Compositional Visual Relations (CVR), a benchmark driving progress toward more data-efficient visual reasoning. Provides measures of sample efficiency, generalization and compositionality, and finds modern models remain far less data-efficient than humans.

publications.title: Understanding the Computational Demands Underlying Visual Reasoning
publications.authors: Mohit Vaishnav, Remi Cadene, Andrea Alamia, Drew Linsley, Rufin VanRullen, Thomas Serre
publications.abstract: Characterizes the computational demands of abstract visual reasoning by assessing CNNs on the SVRT challenge, revealing a novel taxonomy of reasoning tasks and showing how spatial vs. feature-based attention selectively helps the hardest tasks.
